description: 20-highlight eval set for the OCT / grape-attenuation corpus. Each highlight is a passage a researcher might select in one of their own papers. `expects` lists corpus facts a context-grounded explanation should surface that a generic one cannot (cross-paper connections, specific figures/equations, measured values). The judge scores whether the grounded explanation beats the generic one on grounding and cross-paper attribution.

highlights.text: The OCT signal decays with depth according to the attenuation coefficient of the berry tissue.
expects: Beer-Lambert single-scattering model (Eq. 3)
definition of the total attenuation coefficient
link to the depth-resolved attenuation figure

highlights.text: Attenuation decreased with sugar accumulation across all Chardonnay samples.
expects: Fig. 2 depth-resolved attenuation across ripening stages
quantitative attenuation values at 1300 nm
ripeness/Brix relationship

highlights.text: Scattering dominates absorption at 1300 nm in ripe fruit.
expects: separation of mu_a and mu_s
why 1300 nm was chosen
cross-reference to skin/tissue optics where absorption dominates

highlights.text: We fit the attenuation coefficient by least-squares regression of log-intensity against depth.
expects: single-scattering assumption behind the linear fit
depth range used for the fit
sensitivity of the fit to the multiple-scattering tail

highlights.text: The measured attenuation of ripe berries was approximately 2.4 mm-1 at 1300 nm.
expects: comparison against unripe berries
consistency with other soft-fruit values
measurement uncertainty

highlights.text: Optical coherence tomography resolves depth via low-coherence interferometry.
expects: axial resolution set by source bandwidth
why OCT suits berry tissue
link to how depth-resolved attenuation is extracted in the grape paper

highlights.text: Axial resolution is inversely proportional to the source bandwidth.
expects: specific center wavelength/bandwidth used in the grape study
tradeoff with penetration depth
practical resolution achieved on fruit

highlights.text: Multiple scattering degrades the exponential-decay model at large depths.
expects: how the grape paper bounds the fit depth to stay in the single-scattering regime
resulting bias in attenuation estimates
mitigation strategies

highlights.text: Melanin absorption changes the attenuation profile of human skin.
expects: contrast with fruit where scattering dominates
wavelength dependence of melanin absorption
why the same Beer-Lambert fit needs an absorption term for skin

highlights.text: Absorption dominates the near-infrared attenuation of pigmented tissue.
expects: direct contrast with the grape result that scattering dominates
shared attenuation-coefficient formalism
wavelength window comparison

highlights.text: The total attenuation coefficient is the sum of absorption and scattering coefficients.
expects: Eq. defining mu_t = mu_a + mu_s
which term dominates in grapes vs skin
how the two are separated experimentally

highlights.text: Depth-resolved attenuation distinguishes ripening stages non-destructively.
expects: Fig. 2 stage separation
practical advantage over destructive Brix sampling
measurement repeatability

highlights.text: The detected signal intensity is proportional to backscattered light from each depth.
expects: connection to the exponential attenuation model
role of the confocal/roll-off function
how backscatter is normalized before fitting

highlights.text: Berry skin introduces a strong surface reflection that must be excluded from the fit.
expects: depth offset applied before fitting
effect on estimated attenuation if included
relation to the surface-reflection handling in the OCT review

highlights.text: The attenuation coefficient is extracted from the slope of the log-intensity depth profile.
expects: identical extraction method to the grape study
why the slope encodes mu_t
differences in valid depth range between skin and fruit

highlights.text: Sugar accumulation is associated with structural changes in the berry mesocarp.
expects: mechanistic link between structure and scattering
how that lowers measured attenuation
supporting figure/measurement

highlights.text: Penetration depth in turbid media is limited by total attenuation.
expects: measured penetration depth in berries
why 1300 nm balances resolution and depth
contrast with more strongly absorbing tissue

highlights.text: Attenuation values were consistent across the three ripening stages within measurement uncertainty at the deepest layers.
expects: where the single-scattering model breaks down
how deep-layer noise limits the fit
Fig. 2 error bars

highlights.text: Wavelength selection trades off absorption contrast against scattering background.
expects: why the grape study picked 1300 nm to suppress absorption
opposite priority for pigment imaging in skin
shared attenuation formalism

highlights.text: Non-destructive optical assessment could enable in-field ripeness monitoring.
expects: what measured attenuation values would be needed as a threshold
instrument requirements from the OCT review
limitations from multiple scattering
